name: Creality (Shenzhen Creality 3D Technology Co., Ltd.)
subcategory: consumer FFF and resin 3D printers, scanners and laser engravers
origin_detail: Founded 2014 in Shenzhen by Chen Chun (Jack Chen), Ao Danjun, Liu Huilin and Tang Jingke, who met at a 3D-printing exhibition; became a volume maker of low-cost printers (CR-10 in 2016, Ender-3 in 2018).
openness_notes: Initial 0: early printers ran Marlin-derived firmware whose source Creality did not publish; Wikipedia records GPL violations from 2018 continuing to at least 2022. In 2018 Creality published the Ender-3 as 'a fully Open Source 3D printer' (GitHub repo created 2018-06-30, GPL-3.0, with firmware, mechanical, PCB and wiring folders), a one-model opening. For the Klipper-based K1 series (released April 2023) the firmware source appeared on 2023-08-24 (GPL-3.0); K2-series and Hi firmware sources are also published (GPL-3.0), and the Creality Print slicer is AGPL-3.0. No hardware design repository was found for K1/K2 printers, so current = 2 (firmware/software open, newer hardware designs closed, older Ender-3 open).

risk_events: 2018-2022: documented GPL violations involving Marlin firmware and other GPL software
2022-03-25: Artec 3D sued Creality in the US District Court (E.D.N.Y.) alleging copying of Artec Studio code; described as pending
Competitive pressure from Bambu Lab's closed, integrated printers prompted Creality's K1/K2 lines (2023-2025)
2026: listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (per company milestone page), adding public-market disclosure and pressure
robustness: Very large volume (4.4 million printers shipped 2020-2024 per Wikipedia; the company says more than 6 million shipped to over 140 countries) and a broad, fast-refreshing product line (K2, Hi, SPARKX, K3 in 2025-2026); listed on HKEX in 2026. Openness is mainly at the firmware level, driven partly by GPL obligations and community pressure.
physical_science_relevance: The open, GPL Ender-3 is a common low-cost base for lab and teaching modifications (e.g. custom tool heads, bioprinter conversions), helped by its published design and firmware.
openness_effect_assessment: Publishing the Ender-3 under GPL-3.0 in 2018 coincided with it becoming a mass-market, heavily modded printer (about 2k stars and 667 forks on GitHub), and the open ecosystem helped Creality's volume strategy. Creality's openness has been partly reactive: firmware sources for later models appeared after launch amid GPL-compliance criticism, and newer hardware designs stay closed.
key_takeaway: Creality is the volume-oriented Chinese counterpart to Prusa's story: it began closed and GPL-noncompliant, opened one hit design (Ender-3, 2018) and later its Klipper firmware, and used that openness to fuel a huge modding community while keeping newer hardware proprietary, reaching a Hong Kong listing in 2026. Openness here worked as a marketing and ecosystem tool for a low-cost manufacturer rather than as a core principle.

unconfirmed.reason: No page states the listing year in text. The cited about-us page puts 'Officially listed on the HKEX.' last in a timeline whose last year label is 2026, so the year is matched by position only. creality.cn's headline pairs the listing celebration with the 12th anniversary (2014 + 12 = 2026), which supports 2026 only by arithmetic. The linked WeChat article is behind a verification wall, and creality.cn brand news (pages 1-6, 2025-09-28 to 2026-11-20) has no listing post. The HKEXnews Main Board new-listing page (documents dated 2026-06-30 to 2026-11-23) does not list Creality. That fits a listing before mid-2026 but is not evidence for any date, and the archive-page guess returned 404.

Only the cited about-us page names the HKEX. creality.cn's listing headline does not name an exchange, and the investor-relations page shows only section labels ('Global Offering', 'Financial Reports', 'Documents on Display', 'Announcements & Circulars') with no stock code. English and Chinese Wikipedia do not mention a listing, and ir.creality.com does not resolve. No HKEXnews filing URL could be found without search.

The 2018 date rests only on the cited GitHub repository creation date (2018-06-30). English Wikipedia, the about-us page and page 1 of the Creality blog say nothing about the Ender-3 being open-sourced.
